title: Eliminating Time to Derive the Parabolic Projectile Trajectory
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: A projectile is launched from the origin with initial velocity v0 at launch angle alpha. Its coordinates at time t are given by x(t) = (v0*cos alpha)*t and y(t) = (v0*sin alpha)*t - (1/2)*g*t^2. Eliminate the parameter t to find the Cartesian trajectory equation.

steps.title: Express Parameter t in Terms of Horizontal Position x
steps.explanation: Assuming the launch angle is not vertical (alpha != pi/2), divide by the constant horizontal velocity component v0*cos(alpha).
steps.why: Linear uniform motion horizontally enables direct expression of time as distance divided by speed.

steps.title: Substitute t into the Vertical Position Equation
steps.explanation: Substitute the expression for t into both the linear and quadratic terms of y(t).
steps.why: Direct substitution maps the kinematic trajectory into spatial coordinates.

steps.title: Simplify Coefficients to Standard Form
steps.explanation: The initial velocity v0 cancels in the first term, leaving sin(alpha)/cos(alpha) = tan(alpha). The second term reveals that y is a downward-opening quadratic in x, mathematically proving that ideal projectile motion follows a parabolic path.
steps.why: Trigonometric definition of tangent and quadratic polynomial structure.
